   Miss Universe Singapore among 6 beauty queens not competing in Nov 24 pageant in Puerto Rico

 Vion Erico Tan won the Miss Universe Singapore 2026 pageant.

 Set as preferred source Listen Summarise Miss Universe Singapore Vion Erico Tan will not compete in Puerto Rico on Nov 24 because of an ongoing franchise dispute involving six South-east Asian countries.
 Miss Grand International said the non-participation followed “consultation with the relevant parties”, and it does not mean the queens gave up any contractual rights.
 Miss Universe Singapore said it is “deeply disappointing” but will keep preparing Tan for a possible Miss Universe 2027 bid in another host country.
 AI generated
 SINGAPORE – Miss Universe Singapore Vion Erico Tan will not compete in the Miss Universe pageant in Puerto Rico on Nov 24, amid an ongoing franchise dispute.
 She is among six beauty queens who will not be making the trip, alongside representatives from Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia and Laos.
 In a statement on Oct 21, Miss Grand International (MGI), led by Thai pageant director Nawat Itsaragrisil , said the decision was made after “consultation with the relevant parties, national organisations and the six representatives”.
 The six representatives will continue to hold and perform their national titles and responsibilities within their countries, the statement added.
 On Oct 21, Tan posted on Instagram that she had just received the news.
 “Honestly, it has hit me harder than I can put into words. I need a little time to gather my thoughts and process everything before I share more about what comes next,” she said.
 “This journey was never just about a crown or a competition. It was about the opportunity to carry Singapore’s name onto an international stage, to share our culture, our stories and the spirit of a small nation with big dreams. That is what made this opportunity so meaningful to me,” Tan said.
 “I may not know what the next chapter holds, but one thing I know for certain is that this will not make me falter. If anything, it has made me more determined to show the world what Singapore is capable of,” she added.
 On Oct 22, the Miss Universe Singapore Organisation (MUSO) said it acknowledges and fully supports the decision.
 “This development is deeply disappointing, especially for our reigning Miss Universe Singapore 2026,” it said, adding that the MUSO had been getting her ready for Puerto Rico.
 Its statement said Tan will continue her preparations “with the aspiration of representing Singapore at Miss Universe 2027, in a different host country” .
 The development follows an ongoing franchise disagreement, after JKN Universe – which holds the legal rights and licensing to the Miss Universe brand and operates as the Miss Universe Organization – stated in September that franchise agreements across the six South-east Asian nations were not recognised .
 In its statement, JKN Universe maintained that it held all legal authority for licences, sponsorships and franchise contracts . Any agreements made with or through Nawat and his affiliations were thus invalid.
 In response, Nawat – who also heads Miss Universe Eastern – told a press conference on Sept 18 that the exclusion notice had no legal effect.
 Miss Universe Eastern owns the regional franchise rights and a 50 per cent stake in the global brand. The local pageant was run under a licence issued by Miss Universe Eastern.
 In the Oct 21 statement, Nawat’s MGI said: “We believe that women’s empowerment means more than placing the word ‘empowerment’ in a slogan. It means standing beside women when their dignity is challenged.
 “...It means refusing to allow women to become collateral damage in corporate conflicts. And it means ensuring no woman is threatened, rejected, discriminated against or treated differently because of a dispute she did not create.”
 MGI added that it “is not surrendering its contractual rights”.
 Tan, who turns 24 on Nov 6, outshone eight other finalists to take the crown on Oct 13 at *Scape Ground Theatre.
 The remaining delegates from around the world are expected to arrive in Puerto Rico by Nov 8 for rehearsals and promotional events ahead of the 75th Miss Universe 2026 finals on Nov 24.
